plan: Given my value of $25, I need to consider how to maximize profit. Since I pay the second-highest bid, bidding my true value is a good starting point as it guarantees a non-negative profit if I win. However, to maximize profit, I should try to win at a price lower than my value. I will bid slightly above what I expect others to bid, but not exceeding my value. Since this is the first round and I have no history, I'll assume others are rational and might bid close to their values. I will bid my value to avoid losing profit.

I will bid slightly above my value to maximize profit in a second-price auction. Since I have a low value of $3, I will bid $3.1. This strategy aims to win only when the second-highest bid is below my value, ensuring a positive profit. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value.

The optimal strategy in a second-price auction with N bidders is to bid your true value. This is a dominant strategy, meaning it's the best strategy regardless of what other bidders do. Since there are 3 bidders (including me), bidding my value of $26 will maximize my long-term profit.
